newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Changchai expects to exceed 1996 net target.
newsitem.headline: Changchai expects to exceed 1996 net target.

text.p: Changchai Co Ltd expects to exceed its net profit target this year of 250 million yuan under international accounting standards, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
He told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin the profits growth would be fuelled in part by its increased production capacity of multi-cylinder diesel engines. He gave no figure.
Changchai channelled 154 million yuan of the proceeds from its recent B share offer into making the engines. Annual output is now at 10,000 units, he said.
Changchai aims to raise the output to 12,000 units in 1996. Sales would earn more than 10 million yuan, he said.
Set up in 1994, Changchai is China's biggest manufacturer of single-cylinder diesel engines for agricultural use.
The official said multi-cylinder engines require more complex production technology and have a wider profit margin.
Multi-cylinder output would reach 30,000 units in 1997 and account for 10 percent of Changchai's annual profits, he said.

The official said Changchai plans to use 68 million yuan to upgrade production technology over the next several years, with a technology research centre to be set up next year to develop new products and train staff.
Changchai's 100 million B shares were issued at HK$4.97 per share earlier this year and listed in Shenzhen in September.
It said in its B share listing notice that, under international accounting standards, it had net profits of 203.13 million yuan in 1995, compared with 38.09 million in 1994 and 6.49 million in 1993.

Changchai said in its interim report that, under Chinese accounting standards, it had after-tax profits of 125.99 million yuan in the first six months of 1996, compared with 87.53 million in the first half of 1995.
